study_identification_part.si4_title: Detecting accelerated retinal decline in mental disorders through normative modeling

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its hypothesis and aims. It hypothesizes accelerated retinal decline in mental disorders (SZ, BD, MDD) compared to controls and aims to quantify expected macular thickness decline using normative modeling to compare with these disorders.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: We hypothesized accelerated retinal decline in mental disorders compared to controls, with SZ being most affected, followed by BD, then MDD... Our aim was to quantify the expected macular thickness decline... for the typical UK Biobank age-range... and compared it to the decline seen in schizophrenia (SZ), bipolar disorder (BD), and major depression (MDD).

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study describes the reference cohort (Healthy Controls from UK Biobank), inclusion criteria (complete OCT data, quality control metrics, no diagnosed eye disorders), and exclusion criteria (outlier removal). Final sample size is reported (N = 56,545).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: we used these measurements from N = 56,545 healthy individuals from the UK Biobank who had complete OCT imaging data for all retinal metrics... including image quality control measurements... and without diagnosed eye disorders... outlier values were excluded using an interquartile range (IQR) trimming approach
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.location: Methods > Design, setting, and participants; Methods > Outlier removal

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The study built sex- and laterality-specific models and included image quality and ethnic background as covariates. It also modeled age non-linearly.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: We built sex- and laterality-specific models... To model the effects of age on retinal thickness... we used fractional polynomials... Image quality and reported ethnic background were also included as covariates
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.location: Methods > Normative model generation and specification > Predictor variables and covariates

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The data source is explicitly stated as the UK Biobank database.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: This analysis used cross-sectional measurements of optical coherence tomography (OCT) from the UK Biobank database

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: The imaging modality (spectral domain OCT) and specific parameters (raster scan protocol, area, B-scans, A-scans) are described.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: optical coherence tomography images were acquired using a spectral domain optical coherence tomography device, with a raster scan protocol of 6x6mm area centered on the fovea, consisting of 128 B-scans each with 512 A-scans, completed in 3.7 seconds.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: The study mentions the automated analysis software used for segmentation and the outlier removal process.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: Automated analysis of retinal thickness was performed using custom software developed by Topcon Advanced Biomedical Imaging Laboratory... outlier values were excluded using an interquartile range (IQR) trimming approach
nm5_data_preprocessing.location: Methods > Design, setting, and participants; Methods > Outlier removal

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study used 5-fold cross-validation for distribution selection and a permutation analysis (training on 80% random sample, testing on 20%) to check for overfitting.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: we compared the performance of several distributions... in an 80-20 5-fold cross validation framework... To exclude the possibility that our normative model was overfitting the training data, we performed a permutation analysis. A random 80% sample of the HC population was chosen at each iteration...
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.location: Methods > Normative model generation and specification > Distribution choice; Methods > Robustness/sensitivity analyses

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The normative model was built and tested within the UK Biobank dataset. No independent external dataset of healthy individuals is mentioned for validation.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: This analysis used cross-sectional measurements of optical coherence tomography (OCT) from the UK Biobank database

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach (GAMLSS), model type (fractional polynomials for age), and software (R, GAMLSS package) are described.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: we used GAMLSS in R... To model the effects of age... we used fractional polynomials... The normal distribution showed equivalent performance... and was therefore chosen
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.location: Methods > Normative model generation and specification

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Model performance (Mean Squared Error) was compared across distributions using cross-validation to select the best model.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: we compared the performance of several distributions, quantified by mean squared error, in an 80-20 5-fold cross validation framework
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.location: Methods > Normative model generation and specification > Distribution choice

nm11_reproducibility.reason: The software version (R 4.3.0) is specified, and code availability is stated.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: All statistical analyses were carried out with the R-software version 4.3.0... All code will be made freely available after publication... at https://github.com/homanlab/.

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: The study describes the selection of the clinical cohort using ICD-10 diagnoses (F20, F31, F33) from the UK Biobank. Sample sizes are reported (N = 538 total).
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: we then included N = 538 separate individuals from the UK Biobank with a mental disorder... including SZ (N = 171), BD (N = 265), and MDD (N = 102), according to ICD-10 primary or secondary diagnoses

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: The main analysis accounts for age, sex, ethnicity, and image quality via the normative model or linear model adjustments. Robustness checks include cardiovascular risk factors and SES. However, clinical covariates specific to the disorders (e.g., medication, illness duration, symptom severity) are not mentioned as being used in the analysis of deviation scores.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: we used linear models (lm) with the respective retinal thickness metric... deviations as the dependent variable and diagnostic group and sex as predictor variables... we include cardiovascular risk factors... in our robustness analysis

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: deviations from the age-adjusted normative values... are quantified as z-scores, which are interpreted as the number of SDs each individual deviates from the norm... A z-score greater than 1.96... is classified as... Infranormal... below -1.96 SD
